notes.meaning: God commands the seven angels directly from the heavenly temple to pour out the seven bowls of His anger onto the earth. No person could enter the temple, so the command comes straight from the Lord. These final plagues follow one another swiftly to bring down the kingdom of the beast.

differ.view: Believe these bowl judgments describe recurring patterns of trouble throughout church history rather than literal future events.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Teaches that these seven bowls describe God's judgment against the ancient pagan Roman Empire.

notes.meaning: The first angel pours out his bowl onto the dry land. Painful, oozing sores break out on everyone who had accepted the beast's mark and worshiped its statue. Just as they chose to wear the mark of sin, God now marks them with a bodily plague like the boils sent on ancient Egypt.

The second angel empties his bowl into the sea, turning all the water into thick, dark blood like that of a dead body. Every living creature in the oceans dies. This widespread ruin destroys the oceans and shows how complete God's judgment has become.

The third angel pours out his bowl into the rivers and fresh springs of water, turning them into blood. This contaminates the entire drinking supply across the earth. With fresh water ruined, the time left before the final end is very short.

The angel in charge of the waters praises God for being completely holy and fair in sending these judgments. The wicked people had murdered God's holy prophets and servants, so God gives them blood to drink as their fitting punishment. They are only getting what their cruel choices deserve.

A voice replies from the altar in heaven, agreeing that the Lord God Almighty is true and right in His judgments. The altar represents the place where the prayers of the saints were offered and where the blood of past martyrs cried out for justice. Heaven rejoices when God finally vindicates His oppressed people.

The fourth angel empties his bowl onto the sun, causing it to scorch people with intense heat like fire. Instead of turning to God in repentance—turning away from sin and seeking His mercy—the people curse God's name. Pain and suffering by themselves do not soften sinful human hearts without God's grace.

The fifth angel pours out his bowl directly onto the throne of the beast, plunging his whole empire into deep darkness and confusion. The people gnaw their tongues in agony from the combined misery of their darkness, sores, and pain. Yet they still curse the God of heaven and stubbornly refuse to turn away from their evil deeds.

The sixth angel pours his bowl onto the great river Euphrates, and its water dries up completely. Drying up this river removes a major natural barrier, opening the way for rulers and armies from the East to march toward the West. God uses this event to draw the worldly powers toward their final appointment with His judgment.

differ.view: Take the drying up of the Euphrates figuratively as the draining away of the resources and support of an apostate religious system.

notes.meaning: Three foul, demonic spirits that look like frogs come out of the mouths of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet. These lying spirits perform deceptive signs and wonders to persuade the rulers of the entire world to unite their armies. Their goal is to gather all earthly powers for one last desperate battle against Almighty God.

Jesus speaks directly to give a sudden warning that He will return without warning, like a thief in the night. He pronounces a blessing on those who stay spiritually awake and keep their clothes on, remaining pure and clothed in His righteousness. Those who grow careless will be caught off guard and exposed to public shame.

differ.view: Believe this warning to watch points to the rapture, when Christ takes believers to heaven before the bowl judgments occur.

notes.meaning: The unclean spirits lead the kings and their armies to assemble at a place called Armageddon in Hebrew. This name points back to the ancient battleground near Megiddo, famous in Israel's history for major conflicts. There the rebellious rulers gather for what will become the decisive defeat of God's enemies.

differ.view: Understand Armageddon as a symbolic description of the final spiritual showdown between Christ and the world rather than a literal geographical site.
Expect a literal military mobilization of nations in the geographical valley and plains of Megiddo in Israel.

notes.meaning: The seventh angel pours out his bowl into the air, allowing its effects to spread everywhere. A mighty voice comes from the throne inside the heavenly temple, crying, 'It is done!' This shout announces that God's work of wrath is completed and the fall of the enemy kingdom is now certain.

Fierce flashes of lightning, rumblings, and loud claps of thunder fill the sky, followed by a colossal earthquake. This shaking of the ground is greater than any earthquake that has ever taken place since humans were placed on the earth. It brings total destruction upon human defenses.

The great city splits into three parts, and the cities of all the nations crumble to the ground. God remembers the great city of Babylon and makes her drink the cup filled with the wine of His boiling fury. This marks the total and final overthrow of the corrupt world empire that defied the Lord.

differ.view: John Wesley understood the 'great city' split into three parts to refer specifically to Jerusalem, contrasting it with pagan cities and Rome.

notes.meaning: The earthquake causes such violent disruption that every island vanishes from sight and mountains disappear. The familiar landmarks of the earth are flattened and wiped away. God demonstrates His absolute authority over the entire physical creation.

Enormous hailstones weighing nearly a hundred pounds crash down from heaven upon people. Even under this crushing storm, the survivors blaspheme God because the hail is so terrible and destructive. Their continued cursing reveals how hard and obstinate an unrepentant human heart can become.
